slides.title: Operations
slides.subtitle: Confirm exactly what the user approved, at most once, and recover a lost answer
slides.notes: An operation is something a company proposes and performs only once it is confirmed: a payment, an exchange, a cancellation. This example confirms Northwind Bank's proposed payments with the Operations extension, version 1.

slides.title: Why operations
slides.statement: The approval is **exact** and **durable**: a chat message never confirms anything.
slides.notes: Money moves only on an explicit confirmation of one revision of the terms. The user approves in the host's own interface, and the company performs a confirmed operation once, even when answers get lost.

slides.title: Who takes part

columns.heading: Ada and the Atlas host
columns.content: Ada approves in the host's interface; the host confirms with `OperationsClient`.

columns.heading: Standing permission store
columns.content: The Reactor `pap.standingPermissionStore` checks a permission term by term.

columns.heading: Northwind Bank
columns.content: Proposes payments and performs them once confirmed.

slides.notes: Ada is the user and Atlas her personal agent's host. A Reactor contribution holds standing permissions. Northwind Bank proposes the payments; it marks them as not requiring the user's own approval, so a standing permission may confirm them too.

slides.title: Approval, and changed terms

items.title: Proposal
items.detail: op_1 revision 1: EUR 1250.00 to Acme GmbH

slides.notes: The host finds the endpoint only when the bank and the agent both list the extension. Nothing standing covers op_1, so Ada sees the summary and terms and approves revision 1. The bank has since added a fee, so the confirm is refused with terms_changed and the new revision.

slides.title: Confirm, and recover

items.title: Answer lost
items.detail: The bank performed it; the reply never came

slides.notes: The host shows Ada which terms changed and she approves revision 2. The bank performs the payment but the answer is lost. The SDK reads the same operation back: it is never re-proposed or assumed failed, and a retried confirm returns the same record.

slides.title: Exact approval
items: `approve()` records the revision and a digest of its summary and terms
A confirm for any other revision is refused locally: `approval_mismatch`
`terms_changed` returns the new revision and the changed term paths
An agent without the extension gets `extension_required`
slides.notes: Approval is tied to one revision. If the terms move, the old approval no longer fits, and the host refuses it before anything is sent.

slides.title: A standing permission

items.title: Commit
items.detail: A refusal would release the use

slides.notes: A standing permission names one company, account and action, with limits on term paths, an expiry and optional uses. The store reserves a use only when every limit covers the revision, commits it when the bank confirms, and releases it when the bank refuses. A revision that requires the user's approval is never confirmed this way.

slides.title: What stays where
slides.notes: The model can explain what happened, but it cannot approve. Tokens and proofs stay in the host, and the decision stays with the user in the host's own interface. A cancelled proposal's summary says nothing was changed.

slides.title: Run it yourself
slides.cta: The Pydantic AI and Agent Runtimes examples confirm Northwind Bank's payments end to end
slides.notes: Run the Pydantic AI example with PAP_EXAMPLE_MODEL set to the model you want. TypeScript offers OperationsClient, operationsEndpoint and an asynchronous approve, with standing permissions contributed at StandingPermissionStores.
